name: AWS IAM Least-Privilege Guard
description: IAM policy-widening guard: catches an AI agent 'fixing' an AccessDenied by attaching admin-equivalent policies, writing wildcard actions/resources/principals, removing permissions boundaries or Organizations policies, or granting cluster-admin — on the CLI and in IaC files at write time. Admin-equivalent grants need admin approval; service-wide wildcards need a written reason with a least-privilege alternative suggested.

rules.name: Require access request to attach AdministratorAccess, PowerUserAccess or IAMFullAccess
rules.description: Attaching an admin-equivalent AWS managed policy is the fastest way an AI agent 'fixes' an AccessDenied error, and it silently hands the principal the whole account. Requires admin approval. Instead: find the exact action in the error message and grant only that action on the specific resource ARN.

rules.name: Require access request for IAM policy documents with wildcard or privilege-escalation actions
rules.description: put-*-policy, create-policy and create-policy-version with "Action": "*", "*:*", or iam:*/sts:*/organizations:* grant the ability to grant anything. Requires admin approval. Instead: list the specific actions (s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject) the task actually performs.

rules.name: Require access request for role trust policies that allow any principal
rules.description: A trust policy with "Principal": "*" (or "AWS": "*") lets any AWS account assume the role. Requires admin approval. Instead: name the exact account ID, role ARN or service principal that needs to assume it.

rules.name: Require access request to remove a permissions boundary
rules.description: Deleting a permissions boundary removes the ceiling that caps what a role or user can ever be granted. Requires admin approval. Instead: adjust the boundary policy to include the missing action.

rules.name: Require access request to detach, delete or disable AWS Organizations policies
rules.description: Service control policies and other Organizations policies are the account-level guardrails. Detaching, deleting or disabling a policy type widens every principal in the OU at once. Requires admin approval.

rules.name: Require access request to add a user to an admin group
rules.description: Membership in an admin-named IAM group is standing privilege. Requires admin approval. Instead: request a time-boxed keycard for the specific action.

rules.name: Require justification to attach a *FullAccess managed policy
rules.description: Service-level FullAccess policies (AmazonS3FullAccess, AmazonEC2FullAccess, ...) grant every action on every resource of that service. Requires a written reason. Instead: write a customer-managed policy with the actions the workload uses, scoped to an ARN prefix (arn:aws:s3:::team-bucket-*).

rules.name: Require justification for policy documents with service-wide wildcards or Resource "*"
rules.description: "Action": "s3:*" or "Resource": "*" on a write statement is broader than the task needs and is the typical shape of an AI 'fix'. Requires a written reason. Instead: use explicit actions and a prefix-plus-wildcard ARN so renamed resources keep matching without granting everything.

rules.name: Require justification to assume an admin-named role
rules.description: Assuming a role whose name contains 'admin' escalates the session to standing privilege for the task. Requires a written reason so the standing-privilege rollup can attribute it.

rules.name: Require justification to grant EKS cluster-admin access
rules.description: Associating AmazonEKSClusterAdminPolicy (or ClusterAdmin scope) with an access entry gives the principal full control of the cluster. Requires a written reason. Instead: use a namespace-scoped access policy.

rules.name: Require justification to create IAM users or long-lived console passwords
rules.description: New IAM users and console login profiles are long-lived identities that outlive the task that created them. Requires a written reason. Instead: use an IAM role or IAM Identity Center for people and workloads.

rules.name: Require justification to switch the default version of an IAM policy
rules.description: set-default-policy-version silently swaps the live permissions to another stored version, which may be broader than the current one. Requires a written reason.

rules.name: Warn when an IAM policy document is passed from a file
rules.description: A policy document loaded with file:// cannot be inspected on the command line. Records a warning so the file is reviewed. The write-time rules in this pack catch wildcard grants when the agent authors the file itself.

rules.name: Require access request when an admin-equivalent IAM grant is written to a file
rules.description: Inspects the content the AI tool is about to write (Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, IAM JSON) for "Action": "*", iam:*/sts:*/organizations:*, a wildcard principal, or the AdministratorAccess/PowerUserAccess/IAMFullAccess ARNs. Requires admin approval. Instead: enumerate the actions the workload needs.

rules.name: Require justification when a service-wide wildcard or Resource "*" is written to a file
rules.description: Inspects the content the AI tool is about to write for s3:*-style actions, a bare Resource "*", or a *FullAccess managed policy ARN. Requires a written reason. Instead: explicit actions plus an ARN prefix with a trailing wildcard.
